questions.q: Which of the following alcohols contains the hydroxy group, at the side chain of the aromatic ring?
questions.solution:
Aromatic alcohols are compounds in which the hydroxyl group ($-OH$) is attached to an $sp^3$ hybridized carbon atom of the side chain of an aromatic ring.

For example, benzyl alcohol (C_6H_5CH_2OH$) is an aromatic alcohol.

If the hydroxyl group is directly attached to the aromatic ring, the compound is classified as a phenol rather than an alcohol.

Thus, aromatic alcohols contain the hydroxy group at the side chain of the aromatic ring.

Answer: aromatic alcohols$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which among the following compounds has highest solubility in water?
questions.solution:
Solubility of organic compounds in water depends on their ability to form hydrogen bonds with water molecules, the size of the hydrophobic part, and the lattice energy of the solid.

1. Phenol forms strong intermolecular hydrogen bonds with water, making it quite soluble (solubility $\approx 8.3 \text{ g/100 mL}$).

2. p-Cresol contains an additional hydrophobic methyl ($-CH_3$) group, which increases the non-polar character and decreases its solubility compared to phenol (solubility $\approx 1.9 \text{ g/100 mL}$).

3. o-Nitrophenol exhibits intramolecular hydrogen bonding (chelation). This restricts its ability to form intermolecular hydrogen bonds with water, resulting in very low solubility (solubility $\approx 0.2 \text{ g/100 mL}$).

4. p-Nitrophenol can form intermolecular hydrogen bonds with water. However, due to its higher molecular mass and strong intermolecular interactions in the solid state (high lattice energy), its solubility is lower than that of phenol (solubility $\approx 1.6 \text{ g/100 mL}$).

Therefore, phenol has the highest solubility in water among the given compounds.

Answer: Phenol

questions.q:
Identify product 'B' in following series of reactions
2-methylpropan-2-ol $\xrightarrow[\large{363\ \text{K}}]{\large{20\%\ \text{H}_2\text{SO}_4}}$ A $\xrightarrow[\large{\text{Conc. H}_2\text{SO}_4}]{\large{\text{H}_2\text{O}\ \ \Delta}}$ B
questions.solution:
The starting material, 2-methylpropan-2-ol, is a tertiary alcohol. On heating with $20\%H_2SO_4$ at $363\ \text{K}$, it undergoes acid-catalyzed dehydration to form an alkene, 2-methylpropene (product A).

$(CH_3)_3C-OH \xrightarrow{H^+, \Delta} (CH_3)_2C=CH_2 + H_2O$

Product A is 2-methylpropene.

When 2-methylpropene is treated with water in the presence of concentrated $H_2SO_4$ and heat, it undergoes acid-catalyzed hydration. The addition of water follows Markovnikov's rule, proceeding via the formation of a stable tertiary carbocation.

$(CH_3)_2C=CH_2 + H^+ \rightarrow (CH_3)_3C^+$

$(CH_3)_3C^+ + H_2O \rightarrow (CH_3)_3C-OH + H^+$

The final product B is 2-methylpropan-2-ol, which is commonly known as tert-butyl alcohol.

Answer: tert-Butylalcohol

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following on reaction with Grignard's reagent followed by hydrolysis forms tertiary alcohol ?
questions.solution:
Grignard reagents react with carbonyl compounds to form addition products which on hydrolysis yield alcohols.

Formaldehyde ($\text{HCHO}$) reacts with Grignard reagents to form primary alcohols.

Other aldehydes (such as $\text{CH}_3\text{CHO}$ and $\text{CH}_3\text{-CH}_2\text{-CHO}$) react with Grignard reagents to form secondary alcohols.

Ketones (such as $\text{CH}_3 - \text{CO} - \text{CH}_3$) react with Grignard reagents to form tertiary alcohols.

The reaction proceeds as follows:

$\text{CH}_3 - \text{CO} - \text{CH}_3 + \text{RMgX} \rightarrow \text{CH}_3 - \text{C}(\text{R})(\text{OMgX}) - \text{CH}_3$

$\text{CH}_3 - \text{C}(\text{R})(\text{OMgX}) - \text{CH}_3 + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{CH}_3 - \text{C}(\text{R})(\text{OH}) - \text{CH}_3 + \text{Mg}(\text{OH})\text{X}$

The final product is a tertiary alcohol.

Answer: $\text{CH}_3 - \text{CO} - \text{CH}_3$

questions.q: Identify the compound obtained when ethyl methyl ketone is treated with $\text{CH}_3\text{MgBr}$ and hydrolyzed.
questions.solution:
Ethyl methyl ketone is $\text{CH}_3-\text{CO}-\text{C}_2\text{H}_5$.

When it reacts with the Grignard reagent $\text{CH}_3\text{MgBr}$, the nucleophilic methyl group attacks the electrophilic carbonyl carbon to form an intermediate alkoxide.

$\text{CH}_3-\text{CO}-\text{C}_2\text{H}_5 + \text{CH}_3\text{MgBr} \rightarrow \text{CH}_3-\text{C}(\text{OMgBr})(\text{CH}_3)-\text{C}_2\text{H}_5$

Upon hydrolysis, the alkoxide is protonated to yield a tertiary alcohol.

$\text{CH}_3-\text{C}(\text{OMgBr})(\text{CH}_3)-\text{C}_2\text{H}_5 \xrightarrow{\text{H}_2\text{O}} \text{C}_2\text{H}_5-\text{C}(\text{CH}_3)_2-\text{OH} + \text{Mg}(\text{OH})\text{Br}$

The final product is 2-methylbutan-2-ol, which matches the structure $\text{C}_2\text{H}_5 - \overset{\overset{\text{CH}_3}{|}}{\underset{\underset{\text{CH}_3}{|}}{\text{C}}} - \text{OH}$.

Answer: $\text{C}_2\text{H}_5 - \overset{\overset{\text{CH}_3}{|}}{\underset{\underset{\text{CH}_3}{|}}{\text{C}}} - \text{OH}$

questions.solution:
Crotonyl alcohol (2-buten-1-ol) has the structure $\text{CH}_3-\text{CH}=\text{CH}-\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$, which contains only one $-\text{OH}$ group.

Ethylene glycol (ethane-1,2-diol) has the structure $\text{HO}-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{OH}$, which contains two $-\text{OH}$ groups.

Pyrogallol (benzene-1,2,3-triol) contains three $-\text{OH}$ groups attached to a benzene ring.

Hydroquinone (benzene-1,4-diol) contains two $-\text{OH}$ groups attached to a benzene ring.

Therefore, crotonyl alcohol is the only compound among the given options that contains a single $-\text{OH}$ group.

questions.solution:

questions.q: Which of the following isomers of $\text{C}_4\text{H}_9\text{OH}$ has lowest boiling point ?
questions.solution:
The boiling point of isomeric alcohols decreases with an increase in branching.

As branching increases, the molecule becomes more spherical in shape, which decreases the effective surface area.

A smaller surface area results in weaker van der Waals forces of attraction between the molecules, thereby lowering the boiling point.

Among the given isomers of $\text{C}_4\text{H}_9\text{OH}$, tert-butyl alcohol is the most branched.

Therefore, tert-butyl alcohol has the lowest boiling point.

Answer: tert Butyl alcohol

questions.q:
Select the correct decreasing order of acid strength for the following compounds.
a) Ethanol b) 2-Methyl propan-2-ol c) Phenol d) p - Nitrophenol
questions.solution:
Acid strength is directly proportional to the stability of the conjugate base formed after the removal of an $H^+$ ion.

The conjugate bases are:
a) Ethoxide ion ($CH_3CH_2O^-$)
b) tert-Butoxide ion ($(CH_3)_3CO^-$)
c) Phenoxide ion ($C_6H_5O^-$)
d) p-Nitrophenoxide ion ($p-NO_2-C_6H_4O^-$)

Phenoxide ions are resonance stabilized, making phenols more acidic than aliphatic alcohols. Thus, (c) and (d) are more acidic than (a) and (b).

In p-nitrophenol (d), the $-NO_2$ group exerts strong $-I$ and $-R$ effects, which further stabilizes the phenoxide ion. Hence, p-nitrophenol is more acidic than phenol (c).

Among the alcohols, the $+I$ effect of the alkyl groups destabilizes the alkoxide ion. The tert-butyl group in 2-methylpropan-2-ol (b) exerts a stronger $+I$ effect than the ethyl group in ethanol (a). Therefore, ethanol is more acidic than 2-methylpropan-2-ol.

The correct decreasing order of acid strength is d > c > a > b.

Answer: d > c > a > b

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which among the following does NOT undergo Williamson's synthesis?
questions.solution:
Williamson's synthesis is a method for preparing ethers by the reaction of an alkyl halide with a sodium alkoxide. This reaction follows an $S_N2$ mechanism.

For an $S_N2$ reaction to occur favorably, the halide should be primary or secondary (primary being the most reactive).

Let us evaluate the given options:
1. $\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{Br}$ (Ethyl bromide) is a primary alkyl halide and readily undergoes Williamson's synthesis.
2. $\text{CH}_3-\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)-\text{CH}_2-\text{Br}$ (Isobutyl bromide) is a primary alkyl halide and undergoes Williamson's synthesis.
3. $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5-\text{Br}$ (Bromobenzene) is an aryl halide. In aryl halides, the carbon-halogen bond acquires a partial double bond character due to resonance with the benzene ring. Additionally, the $sp^2$ hybridized carbon is more electronegative, making the $\text{C}-\text{Br}$ bond stronger and difficult to break. The bulky benzene ring also sterically hinders the backside attack required for an $S_N2$ mechanism. Therefore, aryl halides do not undergo Williamson's synthesis.
4. $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5-\text{CH}_2-\text{Br}$ (Benzyl bromide) is a primary benzylic halide, which is highly reactive towards $S_N2$ reactions and readily undergoes Williamson's synthesis.

Thus, $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5-\text{Br}$ does not undergo Williamson's synthesis.

Answer: $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5 - \text{Br}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following alcohols on addition of Lucas reagent reacts fast and turns the reagent turbid instantly.
questions.solution:
Lucas reagent is a mixture of concentrated $\text{HCl}$ and anhydrous $\text{ZnCl}_2$.

The reaction of alcohols with Lucas reagent proceeds via an $S_N1$ mechanism, which involves the formation of a carbocation intermediate.

The rate of reaction depends on the stability of the carbocation formed. The order of stability of carbocations is tertiary > secondary > primary. Therefore, the reactivity of alcohols towards Lucas reagent follows the order: tertiary > secondary > primary.

Tertiary alcohols react instantly to form an insoluble alkyl halide, producing immediate turbidity.

Secondary alcohols react in about 5 minutes to produce turbidity.

Primary alcohols do not produce turbidity at room temperature.

Among the given options, tert-butyl alcohol is a tertiary alcohol, so it forms a stable tertiary carbocation and reacts instantly to give turbidity.

n-butyl alcohol and iso-butyl alcohol are primary alcohols, while sec-butyl alcohol is a secondary alcohol.

Answer: tert - Butyl alcohol

questions.q: Which among the following has highest melting point ?
questions.solution:
p-Nitrophenol has the highest melting point among the given compounds.

In p-nitrophenol, there is strong intermolecular hydrogen bonding between the -OH group of one molecule and the -N$O_2$ group of another molecule. This leads to the association of molecules, requiring more thermal energy to break the crystal lattice.

In contrast, o-nitrophenol exhibits intramolecular hydrogen bonding (chelation), which restricts molecular association and lowers its melting point.

Phenol and p-cresol also exhibit intermolecular hydrogen bonding, but the interactions are weaker compared to p-nitrophenol. Additionally, the highly symmetrical structure of p-nitrophenol allows it to pack more efficiently in the solid state, further increasing its melting point.

Answer: p-Nitrophenol

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which from the following is a correct decreasing order of boiling points for following organic compounds ?
questions.solution:
Boiling point depends on the strength of intermolecular forces.

Carboxylic acids form strong intermolecular hydrogen bonds and exist as dimers, leading to the highest boiling points among compounds of comparable molecular mass.

Alcohols also form intermolecular hydrogen bonds, but they are weaker than those in carboxylic acids.

Ketones and aldehydes lack intermolecular hydrogen bonding but possess dipole-dipole interactions.

Ketones have slightly higher boiling points than isomeric aldehydes due to the presence of two electron-donating alkyl groups, which makes the carbonyl group more polar, resulting in stronger dipole-dipole interactions.

Thus, the correct decreasing order of boiling points is Carboxylic acid > Alcohol > Ketone > Aldehyde.

Answer: Carboxylic acid > Alcohol > Ketone > Aldehyde

Pyrogallol is benzene-1,2,3-triol, which contains three $-OH$ groups and is a trihydric phenol.

Answer: Pyrogallol

questions.solution:
The given reaction is the acid-catalyzed dehydration of an alcohol. The reactant is 3,3-dimethyl-2-butanol.

$CH_3-C^+(CH_3)-CH(CH_3)-CH_3 \rightarrow CH_3-C(CH_3)=C(CH_3)-CH_3 + H^+$

The major product formed is 2,3-dimethyl-2-butene.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following ether, on hydrolysis, gives two different products that are successive members of the homologous series?
questions.solution:
Hydrolysis of an ether $R-O-R'$ yields two alcohol molecules, $R-OH$ and $R'-OH$.

For the products to be successive members of a homologous series, they must differ by exactly one $-CH_2-$ unit. This means the alkyl groups $R$ and $R'$ must differ by one carbon atom.

Methoxymethane (CH_3-O-CH_3$) gives two molecules of methanol, which are identical.

Methoxypropane (CH_3-O-C_3H_7$) gives methanol and propanol, which differ by two carbon atoms.

Ethoxypropane (C_2H_5-O-C_3H_7$) gives ethanol (C_2H_5OH$) and propanol (C_3H_7OH$). These are successive members of the alcohol homologous series as they differ by one $-CH_2-$ group.

Answer: Ethoxypropane$

questions.q: Which of the following reagents limits the oxidation of $\text{R-CH}_2\text{OH}$ up to R-CHO only?
questions.solution:
Primary alcohols ($\text{R-CH}_2\text{OH}$) can be oxidized to aldehydes ($\text{R-CHO}$) or carboxylic acids ($\text{R-COOH}$) depending on the oxidizing agent used.

Strong oxidizing agents like acidic $\text{KMnO}_4$, $\text{K}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7$ / dil. $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$, and $\text{CrO}_3$ in aqueous medium oxidize primary alcohols directly to carboxylic acids.

To limit the oxidation to the aldehyde stage, mild oxidizing agents are required. Pyridinium chlorochromate (PCC) is a mild oxidizing agent that selectively oxidizes primary alcohols to aldehydes and prevents further oxidation to carboxylic acids.

$\text{R-CH}_2\text{OH} \xrightarrow{\text{PCC}} \text{R-CHO}$

Answer: PCC

$\text{CH}_3\text{ONa} + \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{Br} \rightarrow$ ?

The reaction between sodium methoxide ($\text{CH}_3\text{ONa}$) and ethyl bromide ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{Br}$) is an example of Williamson ether synthesis.

The methoxide ion ($\text{CH}_3\textO^{-}$) acts as a nucleophile and attacks the primary alkyl halide ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{Br}$) via an $S_N2$ mechanism.

The reaction proceeds as follows:
$\text{CH}_3\text{ONa} + \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{Br} \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{OCH}_2\text{CH}_3 + \text{NaBr}$

The products formed are ethyl methyl ether and sodium bromide.

Answer: Formation of $\text{CH}_3\text{OCH}_2\text{CH}_3 + \text{NaBr}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the nature of alcohols in aqueous medium?
questions.solution:
Alcohols are very weak acids, generally weaker than water. In an aqueous medium, they do not ionize to produce $H^+$ or $OH^-$ ions to any appreciable extent.

Because they do not alter the concentration of hydrogen or hydroxyl ions in water, they do not affect the pH of the solution. Consequently, they do not change the colour of red or blue litmus paper.

Therefore, the nature of alcohols in an aqueous medium is neutral.

Answer: Neutral

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following compounds is obtained by Williamson synthesis ?
questions.solution:
Williamson synthesis is a general method for the preparation of ethers. It involves the nucleophilic substitution reaction of an alkyl halide with a sodium alkoxide.

$R-X + R'-ONa \rightarrow R-O-R' + NaX$

When the alkyl groups $R$ and $R'$ are identical, symmetrical or simple ethers are formed. When $R$ and $R'$ are different, unsymmetrical or mixed ethers are formed.

Thus, both simple and mixed ethers can be prepared by this method.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the name of reaction when phenol reacts with chloroform in aqueous NaOH.
questions.solution:
When phenol is treated with chloroform (CHCl_3$) in the presence of aqueous sodium hydroxide (NaOH$), an aldehyde group ($-CHO$) is introduced at the ortho position of the benzene ring. This reaction results in the formation of salicylaldehyde (2-hydroxybenzaldehyde) as the major product.

This electrophilic substitution reaction, which proceeds via a dichlorocarbene ($:CCl_2$) intermediate, is known as the Reimer-Tiemann reaction.

Answer: Reimer-Tiemann reaction

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of following on oxidation forms propanone?
questions.solution:
Oxidation of secondary alcohols yields ketones.

2-Propanol is a secondary alcohol containing three carbon atoms. Upon oxidation with common oxidizing agents like acidic $K_2Cr_2O_7$ or $KMnO_4$, it forms propanone (acetone).

$CH_3-CH(OH)-CH_3 \xrightarrow{[O]} CH_3-CO-CH_3 + H_2O$

1-Propanol is a primary alcohol and oxidizes to propanal, which further oxidizes to propanoic acid.

2-Butanol oxidizes to 2-butanone.

2-methylbutan-1-ol oxidizes to 2-methylbutanoic acid.

Answer: 2-Propanol

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What happens when phenol reacts with bromine water?
questions.solution:
Phenol reacts with bromine water to undergo electrophilic aromatic substitution at all ortho and para positions due to the strong activating effect of the $-OH$ group in aqueous medium.

The reaction yields $2,4,6$-tribromophenol, which appears as a white precipitate.

$C_6H_5OH + 3Br_2 (aq) \rightarrow 2,4,6$-tribromophenol $\downarrow + 3HBr$

Answer: White precipitate formed

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is a dihydric alcohol?
questions.solution:
A dihydric alcohol contains two hydroxyl ($-OH$) groups in its molecule.

Glycerol is a trihydric alcohol (propane-$1,2,3$-triol) containing three $-OH$ groups.

Ethylene glycol is a dihydric alcohol (ethane-$1,2$-diol) containing two $-OH$ groups.

Sorbitol is a hexahydric alcohol containing six $-OH$ groups.

Methanol is a monohydric alcohol containing one $-OH$ group.

Answer: Ethylene glycol

Step 1: Phenol reacts with carbon tetrachloride ($CCl_4$) in the presence of aqueous $NaOH$. The phenoxide ion undergoes electrophilic aromatic substitution to form an intermediate with a $-CCl_3$ group at the ortho position. This intermediate is 2-(trichloromethyl)phenoxide (A).

Step 2: The intermediate A undergoes alkaline hydrolysis with $NaOH$. The three chlorine atoms are replaced by hydroxyl groups, forming an unstable intermediate that loses a water molecule to form a carboxylate group. This results in the formation of sodium salicylate (B).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Find the order of formation of alcohol from alkene from the following.
questions.solution:
The formation of alcohol from an alkene typically proceeds via acid-catalyzed hydration, which is an electrophilic addition reaction.

The rate-determining step in this reaction is the attack of the electrophile (H^+$) on the alkene to form a carbocation intermediate.

The rate of the reaction is directly proportional to the stability of the carbocation formed.

The stability of carbocations follows the order: 3^{}^{\circ} > 2^{}^{\circ} > 1^{}^{\circ}$ due to the $+I$ effect of alkyl groups and hyperconjugation.

Therefore, the order of reactivity of alkenes towards hydration, and hence the rate of formation of alcohol, is $3^{}^{\circ} > 2^{}^{\circ} > 1^{}^{\circ}$.

Answer: $3^{}^{\circ} > 2^{}^{\circ} > 1^{}^{\circ}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: How many moles of hydrogen are liberated when $6$ moles of ethyl alcohol reacts with sodium metal?
questions.solution:
The balanced chemical equation for the reaction of ethyl alcohol with sodium metal is:

$2\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{OH} + 2\text{Na} \rightarrow 2\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{ONa} + \text{H}_2$

From the stoichiometry of the reaction, $2$ moles of ethyl alcohol produce $1$ mole of hydrogen gas.

Therefore, the number of moles of hydrogen gas produced by $6$ moles of ethyl alcohol is:

$\dfrac{1}{2} \times 6 = 3$ moles

Answer: $3$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the alcohol obtained when aldehyde other than formaldehyde is treated with Grignard's reagent followed by hydrolysis.
questions.solution:
Formaldehyde reacts with Grignard reagent to form primary alcohols.

Aldehydes other than formaldehyde react with Grignard reagent to form secondary alcohols.

Ketones react with Grignard reagent to form tertiary alcohols.

The reaction of an aldehyde (R'CHO$) with Grignard reagent (RMgX$) proceeds as follows:

$R'CHO + RMgX \rightarrow R'-CH(OMgX)-R$

Hydrolysis of the intermediate adduct gives a secondary alcohol:

$R'-CH(OMgX)-R + H_2O \rightarrow R'-CH(OH)-R + Mg(OH)X$

Thus, a secondary alcohol is obtained.

Answer: Secondary alcohol

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The number of primary isomeric alcohols of the molecular formula $\text{C}_4\text{H}_{10}\text{O}$ is
questions.solution:
The molecular formula $\text{C}_4\text{H}_{10}\text{O}$ represents saturated acyclic alcohols and ethers.

Primary alcohols have the general formula $\text{R}-\text{CH}_2-\text{OH}$. For $\text{C}_4\text{H}_{10}\text{O}$, the alkyl group $\text{R}$ must be a propyl group ($\text{C}_3\text{H}_7$).

There are two isomeric propyl groups:
1. n-propyl group: $-\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$
2. isopropyl group: $-\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)_2$

Attaching these to the $-\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$ group gives two primary alcohols:
1. $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$ (Butan-1-ol)
2. $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$ (2-Methylpropan-1-ol)

Thus, there are 2 primary isomeric alcohols.

Answer: $2$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What type of mechanism is followed by dehydration of alcohol to form ether?
questions.solution:
The dehydration of alcohols to form ethers is an acid-catalyzed reaction that proceeds via an $S_N2$ mechanism.

Protonation of the alcohol to form an oxonium ion.
$R-OH + H^+ \rightleftharpoons R-OH_2^+$

Nucleophilic attack of an unprotonated alcohol molecule on the protonated alcohol. This is a bimolecular nucleophilic substitution (S_N2$) reaction where water acts as the leaving group.
$R-OH + R-OH_2^+ \rightarrow R-O^+(H)-R + H_2O$

Loss of a proton to yield the ether.
$R-O^+(H)-R \rightarrow R-O-R + H^+$

Since the rate-determining step involves two molecules (the alcohol acting as a nucleophile and the protonated alcohol acting as the substrate), the mechanism is a nucleophilic substitution bimolecular reaction.$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: An organic compound with the molecular formula $\text{C}_6\text{H}_6\text{O}$ dissolves in NaOH, gives a characteristic colour with neutral $\text{FeCl}_3$ and on treatment with bromine water gives a tri bromo derivative. Which is that compound among the following?
questions.solution:
The molecular formula $\text{C}_6\text{H}_6\text{O}$ corresponds to phenol ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{OH}$).

Phenol is weakly acidic in nature and dissolves in aqueous $\text{NaOH}$ to form sodium phenoxide.

It reacts with neutral $\text{FeCl}_3$ to form a complex that gives a characteristic violet colour.

On treatment with bromine water, phenol undergoes electrophilic aromatic substitution at both ortho and para positions to yield a white precipitate of 2,4,6-tribromophenol.

Thus, the given compound is phenol.

Answer: Phenol

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The molecule with a maximum boiling point is
questions.solution:
The boiling point of a compound depends on the strength of its intermolecular forces.

Molecules containing $-\text{OH}$ groups can form intermolecular hydrogen bonds, which are significantly stronger than the dipole-dipole interactions and London dispersion forces present in alkyl halides. Therefore, alcohols generally have higher boiling points than alkyl halides of comparable molecular mass.

Among the given options:
$\text{CH}_3 - \text{CH}_2 - \text{Br}$ and $\text{CH}_3 - \text{CH}_2 - \text{CH}_2 - \text{Br}$ are alkyl halides and do not exhibit hydrogen bonding.
$\text{CH}_3 - \text{C}(\text{CH}_3)(\text{Cl}) - \text{OH}$ has one $-\text{OH}$ group, allowing for intermolecular hydrogen bonding.
$\text{CH}_3 - \text{CH}(\text{OH}) - \text{CH}_2 - \text{CH}_2 - \text{OH}$ (a diol) contains two $-\text{OH}$ groups per molecule. This allows for a more extensive network of intermolecular hydrogen bonds compared to a monohydric alcohol.

Due to the presence of two hydroxyl groups and the resulting extensive intermolecular hydrogen bonding, $\text{CH}_3 - \text{CH}(\text{OH}) - \text{CH}_2 - \text{CH}_2 - \text{OH}$ has the maximum boiling point.

Answer: $\text{CH}_3 - \text{CH}(\text{OH}) - \text{CH}_2 - \text{CH}_2 - \text{OH}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which from following is a suitable method for preparation of ether?
options: Reacting sodium methoxide and tertiary butyl bromide
Reacting sodium tertiarybutoxide and methyl bromide
Reacting methyl alcohol and methyl bromide
questions.solution:
Williamson ether synthesis is an $S_N2$ reaction between an alkoxide ion and an alkyl halide. For the successful preparation of an ether, the alkyl halide must be primary or methyl, as secondary and tertiary alkyl halides tend to undergo elimination reactions in the presence of strong bases (alkoxides) to form alkenes.

Reacting sodium methoxide with tertiary butyl bromide (a $3^{{}^{\circ}}$ alkyl halide) will predominantly yield isobutylene (an alkene) due to elimination.

Reacting sodium tertiarybutoxide with methyl bromide (a methyl halide) will successfully yield methyl tert-butyl ether, as methyl halides cannot undergo elimination and are highly reactive towards $S_N2$ substitution.

Therefore, reacting sodium tertiarybutoxide and methyl bromide is the suitable method.

Answer: Reacting sodium tertiarybutoxide and methyl bromide

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What type of alcohol is the crotonyl alcohol?
questions.solution:
Crotonyl alcohol has the structure $\mathrm{CH}_3-\mathrm{CH}=\mathrm{CH}-\mathrm{CH}_2-\mathrm{OH}$, where the hydroxyl group is bonded to a saturated carbon atom adjacent to a carbon-carbon double bond. This defines it as an allylic alcohol.

Among the options, allylic alcohol describes an alcohol with the $-\mathrm{OH}$ group on an $\mathrm{sp}^{3}$ carbon adjacent to a double bond, benzylic alcohol requires an aromatic ring, vinylic alcohol has the $\mathrm{-OH}$ directly attached to an $\mathrm{sp}^{2}$ carbon of the double bond, and polyhydric alcohol contains multiple hydroxyl groups. Only allylic alcohol matches the structure.

The classification is therefore $\boxed{A}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following on reaction with Grignards reagent followed by hydrolysis forms tertiary alcohol?
questions.solution:
Grignard reagents react with carbonyl compounds followed by hydrolysis to yield alcohols, with the alcohol type determined by the carbonyl substrate.
Methanal produces primary alcohols:
\($\mathrm{RMgX}+\mathrm{HCHO} \xrightarrow{\text{ 1. Ether, 2. } \mathrm{H}_3 \mathrm{O}+} \mathrm{R}-\mathrm{CH}}_{2}-$\mathrm{OH}$\)
Aldehydes other than methanal yield secondary alcohols:
\(\mathrm{RMgX}+\mathrmR^{\prime}-\mathrm{CHO} \xrightarrow{\text{ 1. Ether, 2. } \mathrm{H}_3 \mathrm{O}+} \mathrm{R}-\mathrm{CH}\left(\mathrmR^{\prime}\right)-\mathrm{OH}\)
Ketones form tertiary alcohols:
\(\mathrm{RMgX}+\mathrmR^{\prime}2  \mathrm{C}=\mathrm{O} \xrightarrow{\text{ 1. Ether, 2. } \mathrm{H}_3 \mathrm{O}+} \mathrm{R}-\mathrm{CR}$}_{2}^{\prime}-$\mathrm{OH}$\)
Among the options, propanone is a ketone and thus produces a tertiary alcohol.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the number of moles of propane-1,2,3-triol formed when $n$ mole of triglyceride is hydrolysed ?
questions.solution:
Hydrolysis of Triglycerides
A triglyceride is an ester formed from glycerol (propane-1,2,3-triol) and three fatty acids.

The hydrolysis reaction is:

$\text{Triglyceride} + 3\text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{Glycerol} + 3\text{ Fatty Acids}$

From the stoichiometry, each mole of triglyceride produces one mole of glycerol.

Therefore, $n$ moles of triglyceride yield $n$ moles of propane-1,2,3-triol.

Final answer: $\boxed{n}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the natural source of salicylic acid?
questions.solution:
Salicylic acid occurs naturally in willow plants, derived from salicin compounds present in willow bark. This botanical source has been historically recognized for its analgesic and anti-inflammatory properties, attributed to the metabolic conversion of salicin to salicylic acid.

Alternative options represent distinct phytochemical sources: cinnamon contains cinnamaldehyde, turmeric contains curcuminoids, and Indian gooseberry is rich in ascorbic acid, none of which relate to salicylic acid biosynthesis.

The correct identification is willow plant.

questions.q: Which from following compounds has lowest boiling point?
questions.solution:
The boiling point of alcohols is influenced by hydrogen bonding and London dispersion forces, both present in these compounds.

Hydrogen bonding occurs through the hydroxyl group, contributing significantly to boiling points. London dispersion forces increase with molecular size and surface area, strengthening with additional carbon atoms.

Methanol ($\mathrm{CH_3 OH}$) possesses only one carbon atom, resulting in the weakest London dispersion forces among the alcohols. While hydrogen bonding is present, the reduced molecular size leads to lower overall intermolecular attraction.

$\text{Less energy is required to overcome these weaker forces, resulting in methanol's lower boiling point.}$

The correct answer is D.

questions.q:
Identify the product ' $A$ ' in the following reaction,
Anisole $\xrightarrow[398 \mathrm{~K}]{\mathrm{HI}} \mathrm{A}+$ Iodomethane
questions.solution:
The cleavage of anisole with hydroiodic acid at 398 K proceeds through nucleophilic substitution on the alkyl carbon of this aryl alkyl ether system.

The aryl-oxygen bond possesses partial double bond character due to resonance stabilization, rendering it resistant to cleavage. In contrast, the alkyl-oxygen bond is more labile. Protonation of the ether oxygen by HI yields an oxonium ion intermediate, which is then subject to $S_N2$ attack by the iodide nucleophile.

This nucleophilic attack occurs exclusively at the methyl carbon, as the phenyl group offers both steric hindrance and electronic stabilization that disfavors cleavage at that position. The reaction therefore produces phenol and iodomethane.

Thus, product A is benzenol.

questions.q: Which among the following compounds does NOT form inter molecular hydrogen bonding?
questions.solution:
Hydrogen bonding requires both a donor (H bonded to O, N, or F) and an acceptor (lone pair on O, N, or F).

Ethoxy ethane ($\mathrm{CH_3CH_2-O-CH_2CH_3}$) contains oxygen with lone pairs, acting as an acceptor, but lacks an H-donor group.

Phenol ($\mathrm{C_6 H_5-OH}$) and butan-1-ol ($\mathrm{CH_3CH_2CH_2CH_2 OH}$) both possess -OH groups, enabling donation and acceptance of hydrogen bonds.

Butane is uniquely incapable of intermolecular hydrogen bonding.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which from following statements is NOT true for phenol?
options: Pure phenol is odourless, nontoxic, high melting solid.
Boiling points of phenols increases with increase in molecular mass.
Phenols show appreciable solubility in water.
questions.solution:
Analyzing the properties of phenols:

A) Phenols are polar molecules: The hydroxyl group ($-\text{OH}$) exhibits significant polarity due to electronegativity differences, resulting in a polar molecule. This statement is true.

B) Pure phenol is odourless, nontoxic, high melting solid: While phenol is a solid with a melting point near $40.5^{}^{\circ}\text{C}$, it possesses a distinct carbolic odor and is both toxic and corrosive. Consequently, this statement is not true.

C) Boiling points of phenols increase with molecular mass: Enhanced van der Waals interactions with greater mass elevate boiling points, a trend consistent across organic compounds including phenols. This statement is true.

D) Phenols show appreciable solubility in water: Hydrogen bonding capability with water via the hydroxyl group facilitates solubility, exemplified by phenol's moderate solubility ($\approx 8.3 \text{ g}/100 \text{ mL}$ at $20^{}^{\circ}\text{C}$). This statement is true.

The statement not true is B.

Final answer: $\boxed{B}$

questions.q: In carbinol system, sec-Butyl alcohol is named as
questions.solution:
Sec-butyl alcohol has the structure $\mathrm{CH_3CH(OH)CH_2CH_3}$, with the hydroxyl group bonded to a secondary carbon. In the carbinol system, alcohols are named as derivatives of methanol, considering the groups attached to the carbon bearing the hydroxyl group.

For sec-butyl alcohol, the carbinol carbon is bonded to hydrogen, methyl ($\mathrm{CH_3}$), and ethyl ($\mathrm{CH_2 CH_3}$). The name is formed by listing the alkyl groups in alphabetical order followed by 'carbinol', yielding ethyl methyl carbinol.

Among the options:
A: Ethyl methyl carbinol matches the derived name
B: sec-Butylcarbinol corresponds to $\mathrm{(CH_3)_2 CHCH_2 OH}$, a primary alcohol
C: Isopropyl carbinol is $\mathrm{(CH_3)_2 CHCH_2 OH}$
D: Diethylcarbinol is $\mathrm{(CH_3CH_2)_2 CHOH}$

The correct carbinol system name is ethyl methyl carbinol.

questions.solution:
Phenol undergoes electrophilic aromatic substitution with concentrated nitrating mixture to produce picric acid (2,4,6-trinitrophenol). Due to phenol's high reactivity, dilute nitric acid causes oxidation side products, while nitrous acid serves diazotization purposes.

B) dil. $\mathrm{HNO_2}$ serves diazotization

D) conc. $\mathrm{H_2SO_4}$ causes sulfonation only

questions.q: Which of the following compounds is formed when ether is dissolved in cold concentrated sulphuric acid?

Ether Protonation with Cold Concentrated Sulfuric Acid

Ethers act as Lewis bases due to the oxygen atom's lone pairs, making them susceptible to protonation by strong acids like concentrated sulfuric acid. The protonated ether forms an oxonium ion, which then combines with the bisulfate ion ($\mathrm{HSO_4^-}$) to produce an oxonium salt.

The product is diethyl oxonium hydrogen sulfate, confirming the formation of an oxonium salt.

Identify the product ' B ' in the following reaction.
Sodium phenoxide $\xrightarrow[6 \mathrm{~atm}]{\mathrm{CO}_2 ;~ 398 \mathrm{~K}} \mathrm{~A} \xrightarrow{\mathrm{H}_3 \mathrm{O}^{+}} \mathrm{B}$
questions.solution:
Kolbe-Schmitt Reaction Sequence

This sequence illustrates the Kolbe-Schmitt synthesis for salicylic acid production.

Sodium phenoxide undergoes electrophilic aromatic substitution with $\mathrm{CO_2}$ at 6 atm pressure and 398 K. The phenoxide ion, being highly nucleophilic due to its negative charge, preferentially attacks the electrophilic carbon of $\mathrm{CO_2}$ at the ortho position, facilitated by sodium ion coordination in a stable transition state. This yields sodium salicylate (A):

$\mathrm{C_6 H_5 ONa + CO_2 \rightarrow[398 \text{ K}, 6 \text{ atm}] o-HOC_6 H_4 COONa}$

Subsequent acidification with $\mathrm{H_3 O^+}$ protonates the carboxylate group, converting sodium salicylate to salicylic acid (B):

$\mathrm{o-HOC_6 H_4 COONa + H_3 O^+ \rightarrow o-HOC_6 H_4 COOH + Na+ + H_2 O}$

questions.q: Which of the following compounds has lowest solubility in water?
questions.solution:
The solubility of organic compounds in water depends on their ability to form hydrogen bonds with water molecules. Polar groups like $\mathrm{-OH}$ and $\mathrm{-NO_2}$ tend to enhance solubility through hydrogen bonding interactions.

Phenol (A) contains a hydroxyl group capable of forming hydrogen bonds with water, resulting in moderate solubility.

p-Cresol (B) also contains a hydroxyl group but includes a hydrophobic methyl group that increases the non-polar character of the molecule, reducing its hydrogen bonding capacity and solubility compared to phenol.

o-Nitrophenol (C) features both hydroxyl and nitro groups in ortho position. The proximity enables intramolecular hydrogen bonding between these groups, which significantly reduces the availability of the hydroxyl group for intermolecular hydrogen bonding with water. Consequently, o-nitrophenol exhibits the lowest solubility among these compounds.

p-Nitrophenol (D) contains hydroxyl and nitro groups in para position, preventing intramolecular hydrogen bonding. Both groups remain available for strong intermolecular hydrogen bonding with water, resulting in the highest solubility.

The solubility order is p-nitrophenol > phenol > p-cresol > o-nitrophenol.

questions.q: Which of the following is primary allylic alcohol?
questions.solution:
A primary allylic alcohol requires that the hydroxyl group is attached to a carbon adjacent to a carbon-carbon double bond (allylic) and that the hydroxyl-bearing carbon is only attached to one other carbon (primary).

Option A: $\mathrm{H_2 C=CH-CH(CH_3)-OH}$ is allylic and secondary.

Option C: $\mathrm{H_2 C=CH-C(CH_3)_2 -OH}$ is allylic and tertiary.

Option D: $\mathrm{CH_3 -CH=CH-CH(CH_3)-OH}$ is allylic and secondary.

Option B: $\mathrm{H_2 C=CH-CH_2 -OH}$ is allylic since the $\mathrm{CH_2}$ group is adjacent to the double bond, and primary as the hydroxyl-bearing carbon attaches to only one other carbon.

The correct primary allylic alcohol is $\boxed{B}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is the structure of an alcohol with molecular formula $\mathrm{C}_5 \mathrm{H}_{12} \mathrm{O}$ ?
questions.solution:
The degree of unsaturation is calculated using the general formula DU = c - h/2 + n/2 - x/2 + 1. For $\mathrm{C}_5 \mathrm{H}_{12} \mathrm{O}$ (with $c=5$, $h=12$, $n=0$, $o=1$, $x=0$), this gives $\mathrm{DU} = 5 - 12/2 + 0/2 - 0/2 + 1 = 0$.

A DU of 0 confirms the molecule is saturated—containing no rings or multiple bonds.

Option A is cyclopentanol, which contains a ring (DU = 1) and has molecular formula $\mathrm{C}_5 \mathrm{H}_{10} \mathrm{O}$, not matching $\mathrm{C}_5 \mathrm{H}_{12} \mathrm{O}$.

Option B is 1-pentanol. With 5 carbons, 12 hydrogens, and 1 oxygen, its formula is $\mathrm{C}_5 \mathrm{H}_{12} \mathrm{O}$ and DU = 0.

Option C is 3-pentanol. Also containing 5 carbons, 12 hydrogens, and 1 oxygen, it shares the formula $\mathrm{C}_5 \mathrm{H}_{12} \mathrm{O}$ and a DU of 0.

Option D contains both a ring and a double bond (DU ≥ 2), with molecular formula $\mathrm{C}_5 \mathrm{H}_8 \mathrm{O}$, which does not match.

Options B and C are structural isomers consistent with the molecular formula.

$\boxed{\text{B, C}}$

questions.solution:
Lucas reagent is a mixture of concentrated hydrochloric acid $(\mathrm{HCl})$ and zinc chloride $\left(\mathrm{ZnCl}_2\right)$. It is used for the differentiation of alcohols based on their reactivity. The test is particularly used to distinguish between primary, secondary, and tertiary alcohols.
- Tertiary alcohols react almost immediately with Lucas reagent to form alkyl chlorides (substitution of the hydroxyl group with a chlorine atom).

- Primary alcohols react very slowly, if at all, and may require heating.

questions.solution:
p-Nitrophenol has the highest melting point among the given compounds.

In p-nitrophenol, there is strong intermolecular hydrogen bonding between the -OH group of one molecule and the -N$O_2$ group of another molecule. This leads to the association of molecules, requiring more thermal energy to break the crystal lattice.

In contrast, o-nitrophenol exhibits intramolecular hydrogen bonding (chelation), which restricts molecular association and lowers its melting point.

Phenol and p-cresol also exhibit intermolecular hydrogen bonding, but the interactions are weaker compared to p-nitrophenol. Additionally, the highly symmetrical structure of p-nitrophenol allows it to pack more efficiently in the solid state, further increasing its melting point.

Answer: p-Nitrophenol

questions.q: The correct order of boiling point for primary $\left(1^{{}^{\circ}}\right)$, secondary $\left(2^{{}^{\circ}}\right)$ and tertiary $\left(3^{{}^{\circ}}\right)$ alcohols is
questions.solution: Alcohols with same molecular weight are expected to have almost same boiling point however two more factors other than molecular weight are important, they are namely H-bonding and surface area of molecule. Both these factors are least in $3^{{}^{\circ}}$ alcohols and maximum in $1^{{}^{\circ}}$ alcohols. Hence, $3^{{}^{\circ}}$ alcohols have least boiling point while $1^{{}^{\circ}}$ alcohols have maximum boiling point.

questions.q: The alcohol that produces turbidity immediately with $\mathrm{ZnCl}_{2} /$ conc. HCl at room temperature
questions.solution: Mixture of anhydrous $\mathrm{ZnCl}_{2}$ and conc. HCl is known as Lucas reagent. Lucas test is used for the distinction between primary, secondary and tertiary alcohols. The tertiary alcohol reacts immediately with Lucas reagent producing turbidity. The secondary alcohol gives turbidity within 5-10 min and primary alcohol do not give turbidity at all at room temperature. In the given alternates, 2 -hydroxy-2-methyl propane is $3^{{}^{\circ}}$ alcohol, so it is more reactive.
